name: GridStor (GridStor LLC; owned by funds managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management)
headquarters: Portland, Oregon (7 SE Stark, Suite 850, Portland, OR 97214); offices in Los Angeles and Denver per the June 2026 media kit
employees: 'Nearly 60 employees' per the company's June 2026 media kit; 68 profiles on the team page (September 2026)
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: GridStor is a Goldman Sachs Asset Management-owned standalone-storage developer and owner that is contracted, not merchant, and multi-market, not CAISO/ERCOT only — the premise handed to this dossier is wrong on both counts and on the sponsor's name. What the company says: 'investment from a fund managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management', credited on its homepage to 'the Sustainability and Infrastructure Investing groups'; trade press names the vehicle as Horizon Energy Storage, and Latitude Media reports Goldman created the company in 2021 after failing to find a developer to back, hiring Chris Taylor to build the team around a Goleta project Goldman had already acquired. Every operating or contracted project has a counterparty: Goleta (60 MW / 160 MWh, CAISO, commercial December 2023) under a 17-year resource-adequacy contract with Southern California Edison; Hidden Lakes (220 MW / 440 MWh, ERCOT, operating since November 2025) with a 100 MW revenue-swap 'Energy Storage Agreement' with Axpo from April 2026 and the balance merchant; Gunnar (150 MW / 300 MWh, ERCOT, under construction, commercial late 2026) under a tolling agreement with an unnamed 'Fortune 500 company'; White Tank (100 MW / 400 MWh, Arizona, commercial first half of 2027) under a 20-year tolling agreement with Arizona Public Service. The company states 280 MW / 600 MWh operating, 250 MW / 700 MWh under construction and 'over 3 GW' of later-stage pipeline across California, Texas, Arizona, Oklahoma (SPP) and Colorado, after five acquisitions in eighteen months from Balanced Rock Power (twice), Black Mountain Energy Storage, Capacity Power Group, Strata Clean Energy and Accelergen.

BACKGROUND. Founded in 2022 in Portland, Oregon, GridStor 'develops, acquires, builds and operates utility-scale, standalone battery storage projects' and describes itself as 'a developer and independent power producer'. Its first asset, Goleta, was financed with USD 55 million of NORD/LB debt (June 2023), long-term debt from NORD/LB and Mitsubishi HC Capital America, and one of the first battery investment-tax-credit transfers, sold to J.P. Morgan (closed March 2024). Since then the disclosed financings are First Citizens Bank's USD 74 million for Hidden Lakes (March 2025), a USD 50 million NORD/LB development letter-of-credit facility (September 2025), Foss & Company's USD 86 million ITC transfer on Hidden Lakes (November 2025) and a USD 120 million NORD/LB and Siemens Financial Services package of construction and tax-equity bridge loans and letters of credit for Gunnar (March 2026). The only battery supplier the company names is Tesla (44 Megapacks at Goleta, built in Lathrop); Enerdatics reports about 120 Canadian Solar e-STORAGE SolBank 3.0 enclosures at White Tank, which neither party has confirmed. GSAM's own June 2026 media-kit line is that it 'has raised over $1 billion to invest in energy storage assets that GridStor will source and manage'; the CEO said in June 2025 that the company had 'deployed only a fraction of the capital that we originally raised'.

Collection gap: no fund name, commitment size or ownership percentage appears on any company-authored page; no EPC, owner's engineer, PCS vendor or O&M provider is named for any project; the Gunnar tolling counterparty, the Axpo tenor, the Oklahoma and Capacity Power Group project names and the status of the 2022 Upstream Energy Los Angeles Basin portfolio (500 MW / 2,000 MWh, of which only Santa Fe Springs at 90 MW has been named) are undisclosed. The pipeline figure moved from 'over 5 GW' (September 2025) to 'over 3 GW' (from November 2025) without explanation.
ecosystemRole: GridStor is what a bank's infrastructure platform looks like when it decides to own batteries directly: a sponsor-created specialist that buys late-stage projects from originators (Balanced Rock Power, Strata, Accelergen), contracts them with utilities and a retailer (SCE, APS, Axpo), finances them with a recurring German lender (NORD/LB) plus credit transfers, and now markets storage to 'utilities, data centers, and other large industrial customers'. For a supplier it is a buyer with a named procurement lead, a stated wait on Treasury FEOC guidance before longer-dated purchases, and one confirmed OEM (Tesla).

productsAndServices.name: Owned and operated storage — contracted with utilities and a retailer
productsAndServices.category: Owned and operated BESS — contracted (RA, tolling, revenue swap)
productsAndServices.description: Four named projects carry the company's 280 MW / 600 MWh operating and 250 MW / 700 MWh under-construction totals. Goleta Energy Storage (Goleta, Santa Barbara County; 60 MW / 160 MWh; 44 Tesla Megapack units; 66 kV interconnection at SCE's Isla Vista substation) has a '17 years contract to provide resource adequacy to utility Southern California Edison' (40 MW at four hours per Energy-Storage.news) and is dispatched on CAISO signals — commercial December 2023. Hidden Lakes Reliability Project (Dickinson, Galveston County; 220 MW / 440 MWh; beside TNMP's Hidden Lakes substation) was bought from Balanced Rock Power in March 2024 as 'up to 450 MW / 900 MWh', built at 220 MW / 440 MWh from October 2024, entered operation in November 2025 as a merchant ERCOT battery, and from April 2026 backs a 100 MW 'Energy Storage Agreement' under which Axpo swaps its merchant exposure for fixed payments and 'pass[es] price predictability through to Houston retail customers'. Gunnar Reliability Project (Edinburg, Hidalgo County; 150 MW / 300 MWh; beside AEP's Closner substation) was bought from Balanced Rock Power in February 2025, signed 'a tolling agreement with a Fortune 500 company' in December 2025, started construction and is due 'by the end of 2026'. White Tank Reliability Project (Maricopa County; 100 MW / 400 MWh; east of APS's Colter substation) was bought from Strata Clean Energy in September 2025 with a 20-year APS tolling agreement, commercial first half of 2027.
highlights: Chris Taylor on the Gunnar financing (March 2026): 'disciplined portfolio growth, focused on contracted revenues'

Modo Energy counted Hidden Lakes ('Evelyn') as the second-largest ERCOT battery addition of Q3 2025 and groups GridStor with esVolta, Intersect Power and Nightpeak as pure-play developers 'scaling after proving models elsewhere'
Hidden Lakes was downsized from up to 450 MW / 900 MWh at acquisition to 220 MW / 440 MWh at construction; no reason is published
Holland & Hart advised on 'a construction (EPC) agreement and a battery supply agreement' for Hidden Lakes (January 2025) and the Gunnar EPC agreement (April 2026) without naming either counterparty
productsAndServices.positioning: Contracted where Spearmint is merchant and smaller than Aypa, Plus Power or Jupiter; the distinguishing feature is the sponsor — a bank-managed fund that owns the developer outright rather than a private-equity minority or a founder — and a commercial team (Titus, Testa) hired from commodity trading and PPA origination to build 'contracted offtake for 3+ GW'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Resource-adequacy contracts (SCE), long-term tolling (APS, a Fortune 500 counterparty), a battery revenue swap with a retailer (Axpo), and merchant ERCOT participation on the uncontracted balance; project debt from NORD/LB, Mitsubishi HC Capital America, First Citizens and Siemens Financial Services; ITC transfers to J.P. Morgan and Foss & Company.
targetSegments: ERCOT retailers and Fortune 500 offtakers (swaps, tolls)
Data centres and large industrial customers (stated target since 2025)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Gunnar commercial by end-2026; White Tank first half of 2027; Birdseye (Colorado) construction as early as 2027 and commercial end-2028.

productsAndServices.name: Late-stage project acquisition — the pipeline machine
productsAndServices.description: GridStor 'both build[s] projects from start to finish and acquire[s] projects midway through development'. The record is five acquisitions in eighteen months, each from a named originator: Evelyn/Hidden Lakes from Balanced Rock Power (March 2024); a 200 MW / 800 MWh two-phase project in eastern Oklahoma, SPP, from Black Mountain Energy Storage (January 2025, sited 'where multiple data centers are already operating'); a 100 MW / 400 MWh Arizona project from Capacity Power Group (January 2025, name and county undisclosed); Gunnar from Balanced Rock Power (February 2025); White Tank from Strata Clean Energy (September 2025, Strata retained 'in a consultative role'); and Birdseye, 199 MW / 796 MWh in Adams County, Colorado, from Accelergen (May 2026, interconnecting at Xcel Energy's Riverdale 230 kV substation per the seller's adviser). In-house development is represented by Goleta and by Santa Fe Springs (90 MW, Los Angeles County, on a former refinery site vacant since 1992), where the city council upheld a zoning determination in January 2024; the 2022 purchase of a 500 MW / 2,000 MWh Los Angeles Basin portfolio from Upstream Energy has produced no other named project. Stated totals: 'over 3 GW' of later-stage pipeline 'across the western and central U.S.' (November 2025 onward), 'over 5 GW' in the September 2025 release, and 'over 6 GW' of greenfield per the media kit.
highlights: The NORD/LB USD 50 million letter-of-credit facility (September 2025) exists 'in support of its development goals' — interconnection and permit security for the pipeline
The CFO said in September 2025 the company had 'taken proactive steps to ensure tax credit eligibility for our project pipeline'
Jack Murray (VP M&A, ex-Cypress Creek) leads acquisitions of 'development-stage and operational projects and portfolios'
productsAndServices.positioning: A buyer of other developers' late-stage projects — the counterparty that Balanced Rock, Strata, Black Mountain and Accelergen sell to — rather than a greenfield originator; that makes it a comparable for how Available Power's develop-and-sell model finds its buyers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Asset purchases from originators (terms undisclosed); development letter-of-credit facility (NORD/LB).
targetSegments: Originators selling at or near notice-to-proceed
Utilities issuing storage solicitations in the Southwest, Texas, SPP and Colorado
productsAndServices.roadmap: Oklahoma two-phase project and the Capacity Power Group Arizona project carry no published dates; Birdseye construction 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Power marketing, trading and structured offtake
productsAndServices.description: Since July 2025 the company has a Chief Commercial Officer, Lance Titus (ex-Uniper Global Commodities), 'to drive portfolio-wide power marketing and trading strategy' and 'contracted offtake for 3+ GW of energy storage to supply utilities, data centers, and power retailers', and a VP of Origination and Power Marketing, Monica Testa (ex-Ørsted head of origination). The first product of that team is the Axpo battery revenue swap on Hidden Lakes, which Titus called 'a major advancement in risk management product development' that 'sets a strong precedent for financeable solutions', and the Gunnar toll with a Fortune 500 counterparty. GridStor does not appear on Modo Energy's April 2025 list of US battery optimisers and operators, and no third-party optimiser is named for its fleet.
highlights: Taylor to S&P Global (May 2026): GridStor is 'pursuing both behind-the-meter and front-of-meter deals with hyperscalers, data center leasing companies and utilities' with Arizona, California and Oregon as focus markets
The Axpo agreement's tenor and price are undisclosed
productsAndServices.positioning: A trading-desk approach to storage revenue inside a developer — closer to Spearmint's merchant desk than to Aypa's utility tolls, but used to convert merchant exposure into bankable contracts rather than to keep it.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bilateral structured contracts (swaps, tolls) and utility procurements.
productsAndServices.roadmap: No announced transaction beyond Axpo and the Gunnar toll.

relationships.note: Goleta Energy Storage uses '44 fully-integrated Tesla battery systems, manufactured in Lathrop, California' — the only battery supplier GridStor has ever named.
relationships.context: The company's project page and its December 2023 completion release both name Tesla and the Lathrop plant; Noozhawk describes the units as LFP. Trade press notes an amendment application in 2024 to add augmentation units. No Tesla order for Hidden Lakes, Gunnar or White Tank has been published, and Holland & Hart's note on the Hidden Lakes 'battery supply agreement' names no vendor.

relationships.scale: about 120 SolBank 3.0 enclosures (100 MW / 400 MWh) per Enerdatics
relationships.note: Enerdatics reports that the White Tank project GridStor bought from Strata Clean Energy is designed around about 120 Canadian Solar e-STORAGE SolBank 3.0 enclosures.
relationships.context: The attribution is an analyst's (Enerdatics, 21 September 2025) and appears in no GridStor, Strata, APS or Canadian Solar release, so it is carried as reported rather than as a confirmed supply relationship. If accurate it would be the design basis inherited with the acquisition rather than a GridStor procurement decision.

relationships.via: Interconnection at the Riverdale 230 kV substation (Public Service Company of Colorado)
relationships.note: Birdseye, the Colorado project GridStor bought from Accelergen in May 2026, interconnects at Xcel Energy's Riverdale 230 kV substation per the seller's adviser Leyline Renewable Capital; no offtake with Xcel has been announced.
relationships.context: The link is a point of interconnection in Public Service Company of Colorado's non-ISO territory, not a contract. Xcel's Colorado resource plans are the natural route to a toll; nothing in the record says one is in negotiation.

relationships.via: Interconnection beside AEP Texas's Closner substation, Edinburg
relationships.note: Gunnar's project page places the battery 'neighboring AEP's existing Closner Substation' in Edinburg; the tolling counterparty is an unnamed Fortune 500 company, not AEP.
relationships.context: An interconnection adjacency in AEP Texas's Lower Rio Grande Valley service area rather than a commercial relationship; carried so the AEP dossier's inbound view shows the site.

relationships.scale: Modo Energy: pure-play developers (esVolta, Intersect Power, GridStor, Nightpeak) brought 1.25 GW online in ERCOT in 2025
relationships.note: Modo Energy's ERCOT annual buildout report groups GridStor with esVolta, Intersect Power and Nightpeak as 'pure-play storage developers' scaling in Texas 'after proving models elsewhere'.
relationships.context: The comparison is Modo's (February 2026), on 2025 ERCOT additions; Engie held about 20 per cent of installed ERCOT battery capacity. Intersect's ERCOT batteries sit inside co-located energy parks, which is a different model from GridStor's standalone contracted sites.

relationships.scale: Hidalgo County peers: Plus Power's Anemoi 200 MW / 400 MWh against GridStor's Gunnar 150 MW / 300 MWh
relationships.note: Energy-Storage.news lists Plus Power's Anemoi (200 MW / 400 MWh), Apex Clean Energy's Great Kiskadee (100 MW / 200 MWh) and three PureSky projects as GridStor's Hidalgo County neighbours.
relationships.context: A siting comparison in one ERCOT county from the February 2025 acquisition coverage; no commercial link between the companies is reported.

policyExposure.exposure: GridStor finances every project partly by selling the storage investment tax credit: Goleta's credits went to J.P. Morgan in March 2024 in one of 'the first class of tax credit transfer sales associated with battery energy storage projects in North America' (Latitude Media reports 'ninety something cents' per dollar), Hidden Lakes' USD 86 million went to Foss & Company in November 2025, and Gunnar's March 2026 package includes 'tax equity bridge loans'. Jason Burwen, now VP Policy, helped shape the standalone-storage credit at the Energy Storage Association.
policyExposure.mitigation: Development letter-of-credit facility and 'proactive steps to ensure tax credit eligibility for our project pipeline' (CFO, September 2025).

policyExposure.exposure: CTO Daniel Dedrick told Energy-Storage.news in February 2026 that GridStor 'pre-qualified vendors and re-assessed supply options during the second half of 2025' and is 'waiting for Treasury guidance before advancing pending procurement decisions on our longer-dated projects', expecting 'a slowdown in prospective procurement and investment decisions' industry-wide and no significant domestic BESS supply before 2028. Burwen expects FEOC-compliant supply to grow (E&E News, May 2026).
policyExposure.mitigation: A 'flexible and forward-looking approach to procurement' rather than multi-year single-vendor commitments (Dedrick).

policyExposure.exposure: Non-residential storage keeps the full 48E credit through 2033 under the July 2025 law while wind and solar phase out, and GridStor's CCO said 'recent federal legislation has only reinforced our confidence' (July 2025); the company's VP Finance framed the response as 'safe-harbouring, earlier procurement, bankable tolling structures' against FEOC, tariffs and queue delays.

policyExposure.regime: California resource adequacy and local permitting
policyExposure.exposure: Goleta's revenue is a 17-year SCE resource-adequacy contract, and its permit trail runs through the City of Goleta (design review 2019, Planning Commission approval of the development plan and conditional-use permit in October 2021 per city records). Santa Fe Springs required a city-council zoning determination. Heatmap reports an October 2025 court ruling invalidating Los Angeles County's memo allowing batteries in unincorporated areas — a latent risk to the unnamed 2022 Los Angeles Basin portfolio if any site is unincorporated.

Hidden Lakes operated merchant in an energy-only market until the Axpo swap; Energy-Storage.news notes the swap addresses the absence of a capacity payment in ERCOT. The company's December 2025 release cites ERCOT's forecast of 'more than 50% increase in the state's peak load by 2030' and 'over 12,000 MW' of installed batteries as the case for Gunnar.
policyExposure.mitigation: Contracted structures — the Gunnar toll and the Axpo swap — in place of merchant exposure.

periods.commentary: A sponsor-owned private company: the only numbers are facility sizes stated by lenders and credit buyers, and a sponsor fundraising figure from the company's own media kit. 'Expected' fields are empty because no consensus or guidance exists.

financials.commentary: About USD 385 million of disclosed debt, bridge and letter-of-credit facilities plus two credit transfers (one at USD 86 million, one undisclosed) against 530 MW of operating and under-construction batteries, all within a sponsor that says it raised more than USD 1 billion for the strategy and has 'deployed only a fraction'. The unknowns — fund commitment, ownership split, Axpo tenor, acquisition prices — are the ones a buyer of the platform would need.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that GridStor is a contracted storage owner, not a merchant specialist, and that the premise handed to this dossier is wrong. Basis: the SCE 17-year resource-adequacy contract at Goleta, the 20-year APS toll at White Tank, the Fortune 500 toll at Gunnar and the Axpo swap on Hidden Lakes are all stated by the company; the CEO describes growth as 'focused on contracted revenues'. Only the uncontracted 120 MW of Hidden Lakes is merchant, and the company built its commercial team to remove that exposure.

(High confidence) We assess that the sponsor is a fund managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Sustainability and Infrastructure investing groups — named by trade press as Horizon Energy Storage — and that GridStor was created by that sponsor rather than founded and then funded. Basis: the company's own boilerplate and homepage, First Citizens' 'owned by funds managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management', and Latitude Media's account of Goldman assembling the company around a pre-acquired Goleta project. Collection gap: no Goldman release, fund commitment or ownership percentage exists in public.

(High confidence) We assess that the growth model is late-stage acquisition — five purchases from four originators in eighteen months — financed project by project with one recurring lender and credit transfers, and that the sponsor's equity is not the binding constraint. Basis: the acquisition record, NORD/LB's four transactions, the CEO's June 2025 statement that only 'a fraction' of raised capital is deployed, and the hiring of a head of capital markets in November 2025.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the markets are the Southwest, Texas and the central grid rather than CAISO alone, and that the 2022 Los Angeles Basin portfolio has largely stalled. Basis: the 2025–2026 acquisitions are in Texas, Oklahoma, Arizona and Colorado; Santa Fe Springs is the only Los Angeles project named since 2022 and has had no update since January 2024; the company's stated focus markets in May 2026 were Arizona, California and Oregon. Cuts against: the CEO still names California as a focus market, and the unnamed LA sites may simply be unreported.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that GridStor's procurement is deliberately un-committed: one confirmed OEM (Tesla at Goleta), an inherited design basis at White Tank reported by an analyst, and a stated pause on longer-dated purchases pending Treasury FEOC guidance. Basis: Dedrick's February 2026 statements and the absence of any supplier name for Hidden Lakes or Gunnar despite a signed battery supply agreement. For a supplier this is an open procurement with a named CTO, SVP EPC and Director of Procurement.

(Low confidence) Trade press and the company's boilerplate say GridStor is pursuing behind-the-meter and front-of-meter deals with hyperscalers and data-centre leasing companies; no such contract has been announced and the Oklahoma project is the only asset sited on data-centre load. Treat the data-centre customer segment as stated intent.

Indicators to watch: (1) Gunnar's commercial operation by end-2026 and the naming of its Fortune 500 counterparty — a slip past first half 2027 would show the second Texas build repeating Hidden Lakes' delay; (2) an offtake announcement for Birdseye (Xcel Energy's Colorado resource plan is the natural route) or for the Oklahoma project — either would confirm that acquired projects are contracted before construction; (3) a supplier name for Hidden Lakes, Gunnar or White Tank, or a post-guidance procurement announcement — the first would close the dossier's largest gap; (4) the pipeline figure in the next boilerplate — a return to 'over 5 GW' or a further cut would show whether the 2025 step-down was a re-scoping or a sale; (5) any Goldman Sachs release naming the fund, a co-investor, a continuation vehicle or a platform sale — the sponsor's exit route is undisclosed; (6) the Axpo swap's tenor or a second swap — a repeat would confirm the structure as a financing tool rather than a one-off.
